From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 20 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Orchid-Plus ingress exception & API shim / vocabulary mismatch

Hi team —

Quick background: Astra Labs wants to onboard "Orchid-Plus" (variant v1.2) into hosted catalog as part of the pilot with VentureEdge (see deal DL-2026-1314). Their artifact looks good on model diff/evals but the tokenizer/vocab size diverges from our canonical token map and KV cache layout. That causes incorrect token alignment for streaming and some prompt-preserving prefixes.

Ask: I want to request a temporary ingress exception (48–72 hours) and approval to deploy an API shim that:
- accepts Astra tokens and remaps embeddings->our token ids at request-time
- preserves KV cache semantics for live sessions (we'd store a per-session map)

Questions for the threads:
1) Marcus — can runtime support a shim without a full variant pin? What are the real latency/kv-cache costs?
2) Priyom — risk of quality regressions from token remap + quantization changes? Any quick evals we should gate on?
3) Laura/Marissa — product/legal: do we need to treat this as a formal pin request or can we handle as a provisional ingress exception with tight telemetry?

I attached a quick CSV summarizing reported vocab sizes and a preliminary compat matrix Astra sent.

Attachments: orchid-plus-vocab-size.csv, compat-matrix.xlsx

Next step: propose quick triage call today (30 min) and then an internal canary plan if infra and ML sign off.

— Diego
Diego Fernandez
Solutions Engineering, Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Dec 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Orchid-Plus ingress exception & API shim / vocabulary mismatch

Thanks Diego — good summary.

High-level product stance: provisional ingress exceptions are acceptable for pilots if we:
- limit to a single region and a small canary (# concurrent sessions <= 50)
- require explicit telemetry hooks (token-alignment rate, fallback-rate, latency)
- put an automatic rollback after 72 hours unless SLOs are met and ML signs off

If Marcus confirms no infra-level cache corruption risk and Priyom is comfortable with evals, we'll treat this as an "ingress exception" (not a permanent variant pin). Marissa — legal, can you confirm whether the shim needs special logging/audit clauses in the pilot MSA?

I can block 30 minutes at 13:30 PT today for triage if that works for everyone.

— Laura
Product Manager, Model Ops
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 21 Dec 2026 08:57:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Orchid-Plus ingress exception & API shim / vocabulary mismatch

Summary of infra impact (quick scan):
- KV cache layout mismatch: if we remap tokens at request time and maintain a per-session token-id mapping, we can avoid full cache invalidation. That will add ~6–12% CPU overhead on the serving node for remap bookkeeping and an extra 8–12ms median per-request.
- Memory: per-session mapping is small (a few KB) but multiplies with concurrency; with canary <=50 sessions it's trivial.
- Correctness risk: the main danger is if Astra's tokenizer produces token splits that change sequence length distribution drastically — that will affect our batching heuristics. We should cap canary prompt length to 2K tokens.

Attached: a quick compatibility matrix with impacted code paths and a conservative rollout checklist. I flagged one blocking item: their embedding dimension matches our model (ok) but the token id ordering differs (non-sequential mapping). That means we must do remap at the embedding/kv boundary, not only at the text->token step.

Action items I'd like from ML:
- Priyom: small eval set re-tokenized via Astra tokenizer + run with our quantized runtime (batch sizes 1/4/16) — check nll and typical hallucination indicators (be brief; 24h run).
- Diego: if you can get Astra to push the token map JSON (token->surface mapping) and a small sample prompt set, we'll test locally.

Attachments: compat-matrix.xlsx

— Marcus
Infra, Redwood Inference
From: Astra Labs Onboarding <eng+onboarding@astralabs.ai>

Subject: Re: Orchid-Plus ingress exception & API shim / vocabulary mismatch

Hey Diego / team —

Thanks for the quick sync. Attaching the token map and a minimal sample set (100 prompts) so you can run the re-tokenization eval. We intentionally kept token ids non-contiguous to support multi-lingual subsegments; apologies for the extra work.

Astra notes:
- We prefer a shim vs a permanent pin because we expect to iterate on tokenizer improvements over the next 2 quarters.
- We can cap concurrency for the pilot and are OK with the telemetry hooks you described.

Attachments: orchid-token-map-v1.json (token map), orchid-plus-test-prompts.json (samples)

Next steps from our side: we'll post the artifact bundle to the Drive folder and ping the DocuSign link for the pilot addendum after legal confirms.

Best —
